name: AION
summary: A British cold-strontium atom-interferometry program for ultralight dark matter, gravitational waves and quantum sensing.
detection_principle: Ultralight scalar fields can alter atomic energy levels and fundamental constants; spatially separated atom clouds interrogated by shared lasers have their interference phases compared.

sites.name: R&D at multiple British sites; Oxford AION-10 approach
sites.location: R&D at multiple British sites; Oxford AION-10 approach

status.label: Prototype experiments / R&D
status.evidence: 2025 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

key_parameters.name: 2025 prototype
key_parameters.value: 87Sr clock transition; reaches the atomic shot-noise limit

results.summary: The tabletop prototype validated expected noise performance; it is not a dark-matter result from the final long-baseline instrument.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
